config.title: Which City to Visit After Berlin - FAQ

items.q: Which city is the best second stop after Berlin?
items.a: **Hamburg, for most visitors.** It is 1h50 from Berlin Hauptbahnhof on a direct ICE and it is genuinely unlike Berlin: a working port, old trading money, the Speicherstadt warehouse district and the Elbphilharmonie. Give it two nights. One night means you arrive, eat, sleep and leave.

items.q: How long does the train from Berlin to Hamburg take?
items.a: **About 1 hour 50 minutes on the fastest direct ICE.** Trains run through the day, so you do not have to build the trip around one departure. Most services fall between 1h50 and 2h.

items.q: Is Dresden better as a day trip or an overnight from Berlin?
items.a: **It works as a day trip at 1h40 each way, but one night is the better version.** The Frauenkirche, the Zwinger and the Neustadt bar streets want an evening. If you only have the day, my Dresden day trip guide has the timings that make it work.

items.q: Is Munich worth visiting from Berlin?
items.a: **Only if you can give it three nights.** Munich is 4h05 each way on a direct ICE. At two nights you spend eight hours on a train for a day and a half on the ground, and both cities lose. If the plan is short, keep the nights in Berlin and take a day trip instead.

items.q: Why does it take so long to reach Poland from Berlin?
items.a: **The eastern lines are slower and partly under reconstruction.** Szczecin is about 140 kilometres away and still takes roughly 2h30, because the trains between Angermünde and Szczecin are replaced by a bus bridge until 12 December 2026. Poznań is about 2h50, Wrocław about 4h15 and Warsaw about 5h25 on the EuroCity.

items.q: What can you reach from Berlin in under two hours by train?
items.a: **Lutherstadt Wittenberg in 40 minutes, Leipzig in 1h15, Hanover in 1h35, Erfurt in 1h35, Dresden in 1h40 and Hamburg in 1h50.** All six are direct. Anything inside that band is a day trip unless you actively want a night there.

items.q: Does the Deutschlandticket work for day trips from Berlin?
items.a: **Only on regional and local trains, not on ICE, IC or EC services.** That means it covers the regional run to Wittenberg or Brandenburg but not the fast line to Munich or Cologne. Check which train class your route needs before you rely on it.

items.q: When should I book the train to get a cheap fare?
items.a: **As soon as your Berlin dates are fixed.** Saver fares are released months ahead and are tied to one specific train. The flexible ticket you buy on the day costs far more for exactly the same seat, and the gap is widest on the four-hour routes.

items.q: Is it better to do day trips or move to a second city?
items.a: **A day trip costs you hours. A second city costs you nights.** Staying in Berlin means no second check-in, no packing and no lost half day around the move. Move hotels only when the place gives you something Berlin cannot, such as a harbour, the Baltic coast or a different country.

items.q: What is a good five-day plan with Berlin and one more city?
items.a: **Three full days in Berlin, then two nights in Hamburg.** The alternative is to keep all five nights in Berlin and use two of the days for Leipzig and Wittenberg, sleeping in the same bed the whole time. The version that goes wrong is Munich bolted onto the end of four Berlin days.
